_meta.description: LLM-generated Critics' Take summaries for shows (concise 1-2 sentence summary, max 280 chars)
_meta.updatePolicy: Regenerate weekly if 3+ new reviews added to any show

two-strangers-bway-2025.text: This charming two-hander rom-com from London wins over critics with its modest sincerity and appealing leads, though some find it slight and formulaic. Most praise its gentle confidence as a refreshing alternative to Broadway spectacle.

maybe-happy-ending-2024.text: Critics hail this charming Korean import about obsolete robots falling in love as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years, praising its emotional depth, visual innovation, and intimate storytelling that's both silly and surprisingly moving.

the-outsiders-2024.text: Critics find "The Outsiders" a competent, emotionally earnest adaptation with thrilling choreography and strong performances, though many note it feels overly familiar and struggles to transcend its source material's adolescent sentimentality.

hells-kitchen-2024.text: Critics praise Hell's Kitchen for powerhouse vocals and Maleah Joi Moon's star-making performance, though most find the coming-of-age story formulaic. Alicia Keys' songbook and vibrant choreography elevate familiar material into crowd-pleasing entertainment.

operation-mincemeat-2025.text: Critics praise this "gleeful" and "zany" British musical import for its clever humor and energetic five-person cast, though some find its frenetic style exhausting and "too clever by half." A charming crowd-pleaser that mostly works.

oh-mary-2024.text: Cole Escola's irreverent farce reimagining Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, foul-mouthed cabaret dreamer delivers uproarious laughs and campy chaos. Critics hail it as hilariously unhinged and gloriously absurd—Broadway's funniest comedy in years.

the-great-gatsby-2024.text: Critics find this lavish Broadway adaptation visually dazzling but emotionally hollow, praising its spectacular production values while faulting it for prioritizing spectacle over substance and missing Fitzgerald's deeper themes.

bug-2026.text: Critics praise this timely Broadway premiere of Letts' paranoid thriller, with Carrie Coon delivering a powerful performance in a production that resonates unsettlingly in our conspiracy-obsessed era, though some find the pacing uneven.

wicked-2003.text: Critics find "Wicked" an entertaining, visually spectacular crowd-pleaser with a powerful score, though some fault its overstuffed plot and tonal inconsistency. Stellar lead performances elevate the material.

hamilton-2015.text: Critics hail Hamilton as a revolutionary, groundbreaking masterwork that lives up to extraordinary hype. Miranda's hip-hop musical brilliantly fuses diverse musical styles with American history, delivering electrifying performances and audacious storytelling.

the-lion-king-1997.text: Critics praise Julie Taymor's visually stunning production as a theatrical marvel, with breathtaking puppetry and innovative staging that transforms Disney's film into spectacular live theater, though some find the spectacle more engaging than the storytelling itself.

chicago-1996.text: Critics praise this stripped-down revival as wildly entertaining and remarkably vital, with its cynical take on celebrity and crime feeling more prescient than ever. The pulse-racing choreography and top-flight performances keep the show fresh.

moulin-rouge-2019.text: Critics are dazzled by the visual spectacle and energetic performances but divided on substance. Most praise the stunning design and pop song mashups as exhilarating entertainment, though some find it exhaustingly excessive with little emotional depth.

aladdin-2014.text: Critics find Aladdin a dazzling visual spectacle with eye-popping sets and costumes, though many feel it lacks emotional depth. James Monroe Iglehart's scene-stealing Genie earns widespread praise in this family-friendly crowd-pleaser.

hadestown-2019.text: Critics hail Hadestown as a stunning, inventive folk opera that brilliantly reimagines Greek myth with gorgeous music and striking visuals, though a few find it dramatically thin and the second act loses some momentum.

mj-2022.text: Critics call MJ a visually dazzling spectacle with electrifying choreography and performances, particularly praising Myles Frost. However, most fault the estate-approved production for sanitizing Jackson's controversial life and prioritizing glossy entertainment over substance.

six-2021.text: Critics praise SIX as an energetic, fun pop concert musical that gives Henry VIII's wives a feminist makeover, though some question whether it's more concert than theater. The dynamic score and performances dazzle, but a few find the concept thin.

book-of-mormon-2011.text: Critics hail this irreverent musical from the South Park creators as hilariously profane yet surprisingly sweet, with smart satire that offends and charms simultaneously through sharp writing and polished production.

and-juliet-2022.text: Critics find this Max Martin jukebox musical a silly but infectious crowd-pleaser, with most praising its energetic fun and girl-power reimagining of Shakespeare, though some dismiss it as unsubtle, overly busy spectacle aimed squarely at younger audiences.

oedipus-2025.text: Robert Icke's sleek modernization transforms Sophocles into a gripping political thriller, powered by Strong and Manville's stellar performances. Critics praise its timely urgency and composure, though some find it overly polished at the expense of emotional depth.

harry-potter-2021.text: Critics praise the show's astonishing stagecraft and theatrical magic, calling it a visual marvel with breathtaking illusions. While the spectacle dazzles, some find the story feels like expensive fan fiction that relies heavily on Potter knowledge.

mamma-mia-2025.text: Critics find this feel-good ABBA jukebox musical as irresistibly fun as ever, despite its ridiculous plot and clumsy song shoehorning. Audiences sing along and dance in their seats to the infectious hits, even as reviewers acknowledge it's far from high art.

stranger-things-2024.text: Critics praise the spectacular technical wizardry and visual effects but find the three-hour prequel narratively thin, calling it an impressive theme-park spectacle that prioritizes sensory overload over storytelling substance.

cabaret-2024.text: Critics are divided on this immersive revival: some praise the stunning theater transformation and Redmayne's performance, while others feel the elaborate spectacle overshadows the show's darker political message.

stereophonic-2024.text: Critics hail Adjmi's hyper-naturalistic drama as a theatrical triumph, praising its immersive depiction of a 1970s rock band recording an album. The three-hour play earns acclaim for its authentic portrayal of creative collaboration and Butler's original music.

water-for-elephants-2024.text: Critics praise the spectacular circus stunts and talented ensemble, but find the formulaic story and forgettable score underwhelming. The show dazzles visually while struggling to deliver emotional depth.

suffs-2024.text: Critics praise Shaina Taub's ambitious, tuneful musical about the suffrage movement as entertaining and educational, though some find it feels more like a civics lesson than fully realized drama. Strong performances and rousing score elevate the earnest material.

the-notebook-2024.text: Critics are divided on this romantic musical, with many finding Ingrid Michaelson's score underwhelming and the storytelling overly sentimental, though the innovative triple-casting and emotional manipulation effectively move audiences to tears.

marjorie-prime-2025.text: Critics praise June Squibb's masterful performance and the play's newfound AI-era resonance, though some find Harrison's 2014 script feels dated or overly familiar now that its once-speculative premise has become mundane reality.

liberation-2025.text: Critics praise Wohl's ambitious, intricately structured play about 1970s feminism as timely and deeply resonant, with a superb ensemble cast. Some find it meandering, but most laud its emotional power and relevance to today's backsliding on women's rights.

boop-2025.text: Critics find "Boop!" a polished, old-fashioned crowd-pleaser elevated by breakout star Jasmine Amy Rogers, though some question why it exists. The dazzling design and tap-dancing charm win over most, but a few dismiss it as unnecessary nostalgia.

queen-versailles-2025.text: Critics find this Stephen Schwartz-Kristin Chenoweth reunion tonally confused, unable to decide whether to satirize or celebrate its billionaire protagonist's excess. Chenoweth dazzles, but the musical feels as unfinished as the mansion it depicts.

death-becomes-her-2024.text: Critics praise this cult film adaptation as wildly entertaining camp elevated by powerhouse performances from Megan Hilty and Jennifer Simard, though some note it lacks the film's satirical edge and fizzles in its finale.

buena-vista-social-club-2025.text: Critics praise the intoxicating music and exuberant choreography, calling the show a joyous celebration of Cuban culture. However, most agree the book is weak and wooden acting occasionally detracts from the otherwise transportive experience.

ragtime-2025.text: Critics hail this Lincoln Center revival as powerfully relevant, with a glorious cast and stirring score that resonates deeply today. A few find the staging sparse, but most praise deBessonet's direction as the right production for this moment.

chess-2025.text: Critics find Chess remains unfixable despite its powerhouse cast and beloved ABBA score, with the show leaning into campy excess over coherence. The performances thrill, but the convoluted book still can't deliver checkmate.

just-in-time-2025.text: Groff dazzles in this slick but formulaic Bobby Darin bio-musical that doesn't reinvent the jukebox genre but succeeds on star power and showmanship. Critics praise the intimate staging and Groff's charisma, though some find the by-the-numbers storytelling tired.

the-roommate-2024.text: Critics praise Farrow and LuPone's magnetic performances in this slight but charming two-hander, though most find Silverman's script predictable and thin. The stars elevate familiar odd-couple material with expert timing and chemistry.

our-town-2024.text: Critics find Kenny Leon's revival of Wilder's classic mostly effective, praising Jim Parsons and its contemporary resonance, though some feel it lacks the depth of previous productions and can't decide on a consistent vision.

back-to-the-future-2023.text: Critics find this faithful film adaptation a visually dazzling spectacle with a show-stealing flying DeLorean, but fault its lackluster original songs and overly slavish devotion to the movie's plot.

all-out-2025.text: Critics find "All Out" a mildly entertaining but unambitious showcase of Simon Rich stories and music that feels random and overpriced, with marketing criticized as misleading about the show's actual content.

real-women-have-curves-2025.text: Critics embrace this crowd-pleasing musical about Latina garment workers as funny, heartfelt, and timely, praising its body-positive anthem and winning ensemble, though some find it leans too heavily into feel-good sentiment over depth.

redwood-2025.text: Critics find Menzel's powerful vocals captivating in this grief-focused musical, but fault the thin story, repetitive score, and heavy-handed earnestness. The high-tech staging and immersive design impress more than the emotional depth.

days-of-wine-and-roses-2024.text: O'Hara and James deliver superb performances in Guettel's spiky, sumptuous score, but critics are divided on whether this harrowing alcoholism tale should be a musical at all, with some finding it a powerful chamber piece and others questioning the form.

harmony-2023.text: Critics give mixed reviews to Barry Manilow's long-gestating musical about the Comedian Harmonists, praising its timely subject matter and earnest performances but faulting uneven pacing and a tone that often feels more like a history lesson than compelling theater.

here-lies-love-2023.text: Critics praise the immersive disco staging and all-Filipino cast, but question whether the dazzling spectacle overshadows the dark political history it depicts, making audiences complicit in glamorizing authoritarianism.

how-to-dance-in-ohio-2023.text: Critics find this groundbreaking musical about autistic young adults warmhearted and well-intentioned, with an exhilarating cast, though many note it struggles with multiple plotlines and leans on conventional Broadway formulas.

illinoise-2024.text: Justin Peck's dance-musical hybrid based on Sufjan Stevens' album earns strong praise as an imaginative, emotionally moving work that transcends typical musical theater, though some find its narrative approach uneven.

lempicka-2024.text: Critics find "Lempicka" visually stunning with impressive Art Deco design, but fault the musical for lacking emotional depth and narrative coherence beneath its gorgeous surface. Eden Espinosa's performance divides opinion.

once-upon-a-one-more-time-2023.text: This Britney Spears jukebox musical about fairy tale princesses finding feminist empowerment divides critics: some praise its high-energy fun and choreography, while others dismiss it as a derivative, heavy-handed mess that fails to justify its existence.

heart-of-rock-and-roll-2024.text: This Huey Lewis jukebox musical wins critics over with its unpretentious charm and catchy '80s nostalgia, though some find the plot thin and formulaic. Most agree it's a fun, feel-good surprise that works better than expected.

gutenberg-2023.text: Critics are mixed on this silly meta-musical, with most praising the chemistry and comedic skills of stars Josh Gad and Andrew Rannells while finding the one-joke premise repetitive and thin over two hours.

merrily-we-roll-along-2023.text: Maria Friedman's revival transforms Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop into a triumphant Broadway success, with critics praising the emotional intelligence of the production and the magnetic chemistry of stars Groff, Radcliffe, and Mendez.

spamalot-2023.text: Critics largely embrace this silly, scrappy revival as timely comic relief, praising the talented cast and Josh Rhodes' energetic direction, though some find the material dated and question whether certain jokes still land in 2023.

the-whos-tommy-2024.text: Critics praise this electrifying revival for its spectacular staging, thunderous sound, and sensory spectacle, though some question its narrative coherence and relevance. McAnuff's production delivers powerhouse performances and thrilling rock energy.

the-wiz-2024.text: Critics are mixed on this Broadway revival of "The Wiz," praising its joyful energy, strong performances, and spectacular design, but faulting inconsistent direction and questioning whether it captures the magic of the original production.

grey-house-2023.text: Critics are divided on this Broadway horror thriller, praising its atmospheric staging and strong performances (especially Metcalf) but faulting its reliance on familiar genre tropes and uneven tonal shifts between camp and dread.

i-need-that-2023.text: DeVito charms in this sitcom-style comedy about a hoarder, but critics find Rebeck's play thin, repetitive, and dramatically inert. Most agree it's a slight vehicle elevated solely by its star's charisma, with little depth beneath the clutter.

jajas-african-hair-braiding-2023.text: Critics warmly embrace Bioh's vibrant workplace comedy set in a Harlem braiding salon, praising its sparkling ensemble cast and humor, though some note the tonal shift when addressing immigration issues feels abrupt.

just-for-us-2023.text: Critics hail Edelman's solo comedy about infiltrating a white nationalist meeting as brilliantly funny and thought-provoking, with razor-sharp wit that balances hilarity with uncomfortable truths about antisemitism and identity.

mary-jane-2024.text: Herzog's intimate drama about a mother caring for her chronically ill son earns strong praise for its emotional authenticity and McAdams' powerhouse Broadway debut, though some find the understated approach blunts its impact.

mother-play-2024.text: Lange captivates in Vogel's semi-autobiographical family drama, but critics find the play itself uneven and emotionally underpowered. Parsons impresses, yet the work often feels schematic despite inventive staging and moments of humor.

patriots-2024.text: Critics find Peter Morgan's Putin drama gripping but uneven, with Michael Stuhlbarg's powerhouse performance as oligarch Boris Berezovsky earning widespread praise while the play itself draws mixed reactions for lacking deeper insight into its subject.

prayer-for-the-french-republic-2024.text: Harmon's ambitious three-hour drama about a French Jewish family grappling with antisemitism across generations earns praise for its timeliness and strong ensemble, though some critics find it structurally unwieldy and overstuffed with ideas.

the-cottage-2023.text: Critics are divided on this Noël Coward-inspired farce, with some finding it a delightful summer romp while others dismiss it as hackneyed and unfunny. The energetic cast and lavish production earn praise, but complaints center on stale jokes and lack of wit.

the-shark-is-broken-2023.text: Critics are mixed on this behind-the-scenes comedy about the troubled "Jaws" shoot, praising the sharp performances and humor but questioning whether the slight, sketch-like material justifies a Broadway run.

an-enemy-of-the-people-2024.text: Critics praise Jeremy Strong's magnetic performance and Amy Herzog's timely adaptation of Ibsen's classic, though some find Sam Gold's production uneven and overwrought. The in-the-round staging enhances the drama's contemporary resonance.

appropriate-2023.text: Critics hail this searing family drama as a modern masterpiece with blistering ensemble work led by Sarah Paulson's astonishing performance, praising its dark humor and incisive exploration of American racism, though some find its larger ambitions unrealized.

doubt-2024.text: Shanley's Pulitzer-winning drama holds up in a strong revival featuring electric performances from Ryan and Schreiber, though some critics feel cultural shifts have tipped the play's moral ambiguity and Ellis's direction lacks energy.

purlie-victorious-2023.text: Davis' 1961 satire proves shockingly relevant in Leon's energetic revival, with critics praising Odom Jr.'s charismatic lead and the show's sharp blend of broad comedy and biting racial commentary, though some find the farce uneven.

uncle-vanya-2024.text: Critics are divided on this starry Broadway revival, praising Steve Carell's melancholic debut and strong ensemble work, but many find the production disconnected and unable to balance Chekhov's tragicomic tone in the vast Beaumont space.

titanique-2026.text: Critics find this campy Celine Dion-scored parody of the Titanic film outrageously funny and deliriously absurd, praising its irreverent humor and committed performances that deliver pure escapist joy over high art.

home-2024.text: Kenny Leon's poignant revival of Samm-Art Williams' 1979 play earns warm praise for its affecting performances and poetic storytelling, though some critics find the dated material uneven and the production occasionally lacking in energy.

job-2024.text: Critics are divided on this intense two-hander about a viral video victim holding her therapist at gunpoint. While praised for its electrifying performances and timely exploration of internet culture, many find the premise implausible and the thriller unsustainable.

once-upon-a-mattress-2024.text: Critics largely embrace this charming revival as a delightful vehicle for Sutton Foster's comedic talents, with strong support from Michael Urie, though some find the bare-bones Encores! staging feels rushed and a few question Foster's fit for the role.

the-hills-of-california-2024.text: Critics largely praise Butterworth's family drama for its powerful performances, especially Laura Donnelly's dual role, and Mendes' vivid direction, though some find the story familiar and overly sprawling.

mcneal-2024.text: Critics are divided on this AI-themed drama, finding it intellectually ambitious but dramatically muddled. Downey Jr.'s magnetic Broadway debut earns praise, yet most agree Akhtar's play raises more questions than it answers.

yellow-face-2024.text: Critics praise Hwang's witty, meta-theatrical satire as sharp and relevant, with Daniel Dae Kim delivering a standout performance. The play expertly balances humor and social commentary on identity and representation, though some find it occasionally self-indulgent.

sunset-boulevard-2024.text: Critics praise Scherzinger's powerhouse performance and Lloyd's bold, stripped-down staging with live video, though some find the relentless sensory overload exhausting and the production style overpowers Webber's uneven score.

left-on-tenth-2024.text: Critics find this memoir adaptation charming but dramatically inert, with Margulies and Gallagher praised for their warmth though the material resists theatricality. The late-life romance resonates more on page than stage.

romeo-juliet-2024.text: Sam Gold's Gen Z-aimed revival divides critics with its chaotic, club-kid aesthetic and celebrity leads Connor and Zegler. While some praise its youthful energy and sexy staging, many find it aggressively gimmicky and emotionally hollow.

a-wonderful-world-the-louis-armstrong-mu.text: Critics find this Armstrong bio-musical musically rich but narratively overstuffed, with James Monroe Iglehart's impressive performance and the four actresses playing Armstrong's wives nearly overshadowed by a conventional, information-heavy book.

tammy-faye-2024.text: Critics find "Tammy Faye" tonally confused and messy, struggling between camp, satire, and sincerity. Katie Brayben's powerhouse performance earns praise, but Elton John's score and the muddled book disappoint in this splashy yet shallow spectacle.

elf-2024.text: This crowd-pleasing holiday revival delivers sugar-rush cheer with Grey Henson's winning performance, though critics note forgettable songs and one-joke plotting make it more ho-ho-hum than magical.

swept-away-2024.text: Critics find this Avett Brothers musical about shipwrecked sailors beautifully staged and performed, but many feel it's more emotionally distant than engrossing, with a grim story that can feel sleepy despite strong production values.

cult-of-love-2024.text: Headland's darkly funny family drama about holiday dysfunction earns praise for its sharp writing and strong ensemble cast, though some critics find it overstuffed with issues. The festive setting and biting humor resonate, even when veering into melodrama.

eureka-day-2024.text: Critics praise Spector's sharp satire of progressive parents clashing over vaccines as hilarious and uncomfortably timely, though some find its characters cartoonish. A stellar ensemble and a standout Zoom scene earn widespread acclaim.

gypsy-2024.text: Critics hail McDonald's grounded, emotionally nuanced Rose as a revelation, bringing fresh depth to the iconic role. While most praise Wolfe's moving revival of the classic musical, some find the production slow-paced and uneven.

all-in-comedy-about-love-2024.text: Critics are mixed on this celebrity-studded staged reading of Simon Rich's short stories, with some charmed by the gentle wit and star power while others dismiss it as an overpriced, underrehearsed cash grab masquerading as a Broadway play.

english-2025.text: Toossi's Pulitzer-winning play about Iranians learning English earns widespread praise for its subtle, moving exploration of language and identity. Critics laud the performances and thematic depth, though some find the pacing slow and undramatic.

purpose-2025.text: Critics praise Jacobs-Jenkins' sharp, witty family drama about a prominent Black family's secrets, though most agree the strong first act outpaces a slower second. Rashad's direction and the ensemble earn acclaim.

othello-2025.text: Washington and Gyllenhaal's star power draws record crowds, but critics find Leon's production disappointingly underpowered and lacking vision, with performances that fail to unlock Shakespeare's tragedy.

the-picture-of-dorian-gray-2025.text: Sarah Snook dazzles in a technically ingenious one-woman tour de force, playing 26 characters amid elaborate video technology. Critics praise her virtuosity but divide on whether the tech enhances or overwhelms Wilde's story.

glengarry-glen-ross-2025.text: Mamet's savage play crackles with a starry cast led by Culkin, Odenkirk, and Burr, but critics are divided on whether this slick revival justifies another trip to the well—or its premium prices at the oversized Palace Theatre.

good-night-and-good-luck-2025.text: Critics are mixed on Clooney's timely Broadway debut as Edward R. Murrow. While many praise the production's urgency and ensemble work, others find it a too-faithful film adaptation that feels stiff, preachy, and lacking theatrical spark.

the-last-five-years-2025.text: Brown's beloved score shines in its Broadway debut, but the intimate two-hander struggles with an overproduced staging. Warren dazzles, Jonas underwhelms, and the show's structural conceits don't fully land.

stephen-sondheims-old-friends-2025.text: Critics find this Sondheim revue a pleasant if uneven celebration, elevated by stellar performers like Bernadette Peters and Lea Salonga delivering brilliant songs, though some question whether Broadway needs another tribute show.

john-proctor-is-the-villain-2025.text: Critics praise this sharp, timely reimagining of "The Crucible" through a #MeToo lens, lauding Belflower's witty writing and youthful energy. Some find it overly didactic or contrived, but most celebrate its vital feminist perspective and strong performances.

floyd-collins-2025.text: Critics find this chamber musical's Broadway debut mostly beautiful but uneven, praising Guettel's score and Jordan's performance while noting the production struggles to convey claustrophobia and emotional depth on the vast stage.

pirates-the-penzance-musical-2025.text: Critics warmly embrace this New Orleans-set reimagining of Gilbert & Sullivan's classic, praising its charm and energetic performances, particularly David Hyde Pierce's patter song mastery, though purists may need time to adjust to the liberties taken.

dead-outlaw-2025.text: Critics praise this darkly inventive musical about outlaw Elmer McCurdy's bizarre afterlife as wildly entertaining and uniquely original, with a standout rockabilly score and Andrew Durand's remarkable performance as a corpse stealing the show.

the-kite-runner-2022.text: Critics are divided on this faithful adaptation of Hosseini's beloved novel, with many finding it earnest but earthbound. While the cast earns praise, the production struggles with clunky staging and excessive narration that fails to soar theatrically.

into-the-woods-2022.text: Critics hail this stripped-down revival as a triumphant tribute to Sondheim, with an exceptional cast and crystalline staging that lets the score shine. The pared-back approach proves enchanting, though some find the concert staging unremarkable.

leopoldstadt-2022.text: Stoppard's deeply personal Holocaust drama earns widespread acclaim as a moving meditation on memory and Jewish identity, though some find its sprawling multi-generational structure and large cast difficult to follow.

cost-of-living-2022.text: Majok's Pulitzer-winning drama earns strong praise for its unsentimental exploration of disability and caregiving, anchored by exceptional performances. Critics laud its intimacy and compassion, though some find it occasionally cloying.

1776-2022.text: This diverse, all-female/trans/nonbinary revival of the 1969 musical earns mixed-to-positive reviews for its vibrant cast and bold reimagining, though critics split on whether the high-concept casting and heavy-handed direction truly reinvigorate the material.

death-of-a-salesman-2022.text: Critics praise this historic revival with a Black Loman family, led by Wendell Pierce's powerful Willy and Sharon D. Clarke's standout Linda. Some find directorial choices distracting, but strong performances and fresh racial insights revitalize Miller's classic.

the-piano-lesson-2022.text: Critics find this starry revival of Wilson's Pulitzer winner mostly compelling but tonally uneven, with some praising its emotional power and direction while others cite pacing issues and an overemphasis on horror elements over metaphor.

topdog-underdog-2022.text: Parks' Pulitzer-winning play crackles with electric vitality in this acclaimed revival, powered by powerhouse performances from Hawkins and Abdul-Mateen II that bring fresh urgency to the timeless sibling drama.

walking-with-ghosts-2022.text: Byrne's storytelling charms in this memoir adaptation, though critics split on whether his poetic reminiscences justify a full Broadway evening. His wit and stage presence captivate, but some find the intimate material better suited to a smaller venue.

almost-famous-2022.text: Mixed reviews greet this rock musical adaptation, with critics praising Casey Likes' performance and some heartfelt moments, but faulting lackluster songs and a sanitized approach that fails to capture the film's magic.

kimberly-akimbo-2022.text: Critics hail this quirky musical as a small miracle that balances heartbreak and humor with perfect tonal control. Praised for its originality, emotional depth, and Victoria Clark's performance, it's called refreshingly intimate and deeply moving.

take-me-out-2022.text: Greenberg's 20-year-old play about a gay baseball star coming out feels both timely and dated, but strong performances—especially Ferguson's—and sharp direction elevate this well-crafted, if occasionally overlong, drama.

mike-birbiglia-the-old-man-and-the-pool-.text: Critics praise Birbiglia's masterful storytelling as he mines his health scare for both hilarious and genuinely moving reflections on mortality, though some find his formula overly familiar and predictable.

a-christmas-carol-2022.text: Critics are divided on this technically dazzling production. Jefferson Mays' virtuosic 50-character solo performance and stunning stagecraft earn praise, but some find the adaptation emotionally hollow, prioritizing spectacle over Scrooge's transformation.

kpop-2022.text: Critics praise KPOP's electrifying choreography and high-energy performances, but most find the book thin and dramatically inert. The spectacle dazzles, yet the show struggles to match its visual polish with compelling storytelling.

aint-no-mo-2022.text: Critics praise Jordan E. Cooper's audacious satire as a raucous, boundary-pushing examination of Black American life that's both hilarious and heartbreaking, though some find it uneven. The performances and fearless irreverence earn widespread acclaim.

a-beautiful-noise-the-neil-diamond-music.text: Critics find this Neil Diamond jukebox musical delivers crowd-pleasing hits with strong vocal performances, particularly from lead Nick Fradiani, but suffers from a thin, formulaic book that superficially explores Diamond's life through an unnecessary therapy framing device.

ohio-state-murders-2022.text: Critics praise Audra McDonald's mesmerizing, masterful performance in Adrienne Kennedy's belated Broadway debut, a brief but powerful exploration of racial violence that leaves a haunting impact, though some find the production overly reverential.

some-like-it-hot-2022.text: Critics praise this fizzy, crowd-pleasing adaptation for its dazzling choreography and stellar performances, though some find the score derivative and the updated gender politics heavy-handed.

the-collaboration-2022.text: Mixed reviews praise Bettany and Pope's magnetic performances as Warhol and Basquiat, but critics find McCarten's bioplay dramatically inert, lacking conflict and depth despite exploring their intriguing 1980s artistic partnership.

between-riverside-and-crazy-2022.text: Guirgis's Pulitzer winner earns widespread praise for Stephen McKinley Henderson's powerhouse lead performance and sharp, vibrant dialogue, though a few critics find the supporting cast uneven and the production's impact diminished since its Off-Broadway debut.

pictures-from-home-2023.text: Critics find this family drama elevated by stellar performances from Lane, Burstein, and Wanamaker, but fault White's adaptation for being verbose and underdeveloped, struggling to capture the subtlety of Sultan's photo memoir.

a-dolls-house-2023.text: Lloyd's ultra-minimalist staging and Chastain's compelling performance polarize critics: some find the stripped-down, podcast-like approach hypnotic and stunning, while others feel it drains Ibsen's drama of vitality and emotion.

parade-2023.text: This acclaimed revival of the 1998 musical about Leo Frank's lynching feels urgently relevant, elevated by powerhouse performances from Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond and Jason Robert Brown's stunning score.

bob-fosses-dancin-2023.text: Critics praise the athletic virtuosity and electric energy of the 16-member ensemble, though some find the plotless revue more style showcase than substantive theater, with debate over whether it honors or dilutes Fosse's legacy.

bad-cinderella-2023.text: Critics lambast Lloyd Webber's fairy tale update as confused, crass, and rudderless, with most finding it loud, tasteless, and lacking coherent vision. Carolee Carmello's stepmother performance earns scattered praise amid the chaos.

sweeney-todd-2023.text: Critics praise this full-scale revival for its vocal power and lush orchestrations, with Groban and Ashford earning strong notices. Kail's production impresses with its grand ambition, though some find it lacks the visceral edge of past versions.

life-of-pi-2023.text: Critics praise Life of Pi as a visually stunning theatrical spectacle with extraordinary puppetry, particularly the Bengal tiger Richard Parker, though some find the script uneven and less emotionally resonant than its dazzling stagecraft.

shucked-2023.text: Critics find this aggressively corny musical comedy surprisingly funny and good-natured, praising its rapid-fire puns and catchy country score, though some note the thin plot and relentless jokes can wear thin despite the cast's infectious enthusiasm.

fat-ham-2023.text: Critics praise this Pulitzer-winning Hamlet reimagining set at a Black family barbecue as raucous, funny, and moving, with standout performances. Some find it occasionally strains under its ambitions, but most celebrate its fresh take on toxic masculinity and cycles of violence.

camelot-2023.text: Sorkin's revised "Camelot" strips away the magic and fantasy, yielding mixed results: critics praise the lush score and talented cast (especially Soo and Donica), but find the darker, politically modernized approach less enchanting than hoped.

peter-pan-goes-wrong-2023.text: Critics largely embrace this slapstick farce about a disastrous amateur production, praising its technical precision and broad physical comedy, though some find the repetitive mayhem exhausting over two hours.

the-thanksgiving-play-2023.text: FastHorse's satire of performatively woke white liberals devising a culturally sensitive Thanksgiving play earns laughs but draws mixed reviews, with some finding it sharp and timely while others feel its 2015-era humor has aged poorly.

prima-facie-2023.text: Critics hail Jodie Comer's "extraordinary" and "stunning" Broadway debut in this one-woman legal thriller about sexual assault, though some find Suzie Miller's play overly didactic or schematic despite its urgent, timely subject matter.

good-night-oscar-2023.text: Hayes delivers a tour-de-force performance as troubled pianist Oscar Levant, but critics are divided on Wright's biographical play, with some finding it a captivating character study and others criticizing its exposition-heavy script.

summer-1976-2023.text: Critics find Auburn's intimate two-hander a gentle, largely uneventful memory play elevated by masterful performances from Linney and Hecht, though many wish the thin material matched the caliber of its stars.

new-york-new-york-2023.text: A sprawling, unfocused love letter to the city that fails to capture its magic. Despite Stroman's dazzling choreography and a legendary Kander & Ebb score, the show feels long-winded, overstuffed, and surprisingly dull.

the-sign-in-sidney-brusteins-window-2023.text: Critics are divided on Hansberry's sprawling, verbose play about 1960s Greenwich Village idealism, with some finding it brilliant and others calling it unfocused. Isaac and Brosnahan's performances earn consistent praise.

pass-over-2021.text: Critics praise this urgent, powerful Godot-inspired drama about Black experience in America as a bold Broadway reopening, lauding Hill and Smallwood's chemistry and Nwandu's blend of bleak humor with unflinching social commentary.

waitress-2021.text: Critics praise Jessie Mueller's transcendent performance and Sara Bareilles' appealing pop score, but find the musical overly sweet and formulaic. The show charms with its warmth and all-female creative team, though some cite a predictable book and broad characterizations.

lackawanna-blues-2021.text: Santiago-Hudson delivers a virtuosic performance in this warmly nostalgic solo show, inhabiting two dozen characters from his childhood with impressive skill, though some critics find the autobiographical memory play more self-indulgent than essential.

chicken-and-biscuits-2021.text: Critics find this family funeral comedy warmly performed and crowd-pleasing, but formulaic and uneven. The broad humor and heartfelt performances mostly compensate for sitcom-level writing and a structure that loses steam.

is-this-a-room-2021.text: Critics praise this verbatim FBI transcript as a gripping, anxiety-inducing thriller that transforms a government document into taut, compelling theater, though some find it unsettling and unresolved.

thoughts-of-a-colored-man-2021.text: Critics find Scott's portrait of seven Black men in Brooklyn ambitious and timely, praising its vibrant cast and authentic voices, though many note its episodic structure feels uneven and more like connected monologues than a fully cohesive play.

the-lehman-trilogy-2021.text: Critics hail this epic three-and-a-half-hour drama as a theatrical triumph, praising Mendes' direction and three extraordinary actors who bring 164 years of American capitalism to vivid life, though some find it historically blinkered or self-important.

dana-h-2021.text: Critics hail this documentary thriller as unlike anything on Broadway, with Deirdre O'Connell delivering an extraordinary performance lip-syncing playwright Lucas Hnath's mother recounting her harrowing five-month abduction.

caroline-or-change-2021.text: Critics hail this overdue revival as timely and necessary, with Sharon D Clarke delivering a towering, transcendent performance. The ambitious Kushner-Tesori musical divides some with its unconventional structure, but most find it deeply moving.

diana-the-musical-2021.text: Critics savage this Princess Diana musical as tasteless, tone-deaf, and superficial, with terrible songs and lyrics that reduce a tragic figure to campy melodrama. A few find it entertaining schlock, but most call it ghoulish exploitation.

trouble-in-mind-2021.text: Childress's 1955 satire about racism in theater finally reaches Broadway 65+ years late and feels remarkably timely. Critics praise LaChanze's powerhouse lead performance and the play's prescient examination of racial inequity, though some find it uneven.

clydes-2021.text: Lynn Nottage's warmhearted comedy about ex-cons finding redemption in a truck-stop sandwich shop earns praise for its humor and stellar performances, especially Uzo Aduba, though some critics find it slight compared to her weightier work.

slave-play-2021.text: Critics are divided on Harris's provocative exploration of race and sex: some praise its daring confrontation of slavery's legacy and stellar performances, while others find it overly conceptual and dramatically messy despite its shock value.

company-2021.text: Elliott's gender-flipped revival of Sondheim's "Company" earns mostly strong praise for its fresh, vital reinvention, with standout performances from Lenk and LuPone, though some critics question whether the changes fully work.

flying-over-sunset-2021.text: Critics find this LSD-themed musical about Cary Grant, Aldous Huxley, and Clare Boothe Luce mostly dull and disconnected, though some praise Tony Yazbeck's dazzling tap dancing and the striking visual design.

skeleton-crew-2022.text: Morisseau's compassionate drama about Detroit auto workers facing economic uncertainty earns praise for its authentic sense of place, eloquent writing, and strong performances, especially Phylicia Rashad's, though some find it stronger on atmosphere than dramatic tension.

the-music-man-2022.text: Critics are divided on this starry revival: Jackman and Foster's charisma dazzles, but many find the production surprisingly flat and overly safe, failing to live up to its blockbuster hype despite polished performances and spectacle.

plaza-suite-2022.text: Critics are divided on this Neil Simon revival, with many finding the 1968 material dated despite Parker and Broderick's charming chemistry and comic timing delivering crowd-pleasing laughs.

paradise-square-2022.text: Critics find Paradise Square an ambitious but overstuffed musical about Civil War-era New York, praising Joaquina Kalukango's powerhouse performance and Bill T. Jones's thrilling choreography while faulting its sprawling, unfocused book.

beetlejuice-2022.text: Critics find "Beetlejuice" a visually spectacular, high-energy spectacle with standout performances and clever humor, though some cite sensory overload and forgettable songs. The show divides audiences but delivers irreverent fun for fans of Burton's aesthetic.

birthday-candles-2022.text: Critics are divided on this life-spanning dramedy, with some finding it poignant and others dismissing it as treacly and clichéd. Messing's performance earns praise, but many feel the play's cosmic themes amount to manipulative fluff.

american-buffalo-2022.text: Critics find Mamet's 1975 play feels dated, but Rockwell, Fishburne, and Criss deliver powerhouse performances that elevate the profanity-laden material into a compelling acting showcase, even if the text's relevance has diminished.

the-minutes-2022.text: Letts' darkly comic city council drama starts as mundane satire before delivering a disturbing gut-punch about America's buried history. Critics praise the sharp writing and performances, though some find the shocking finale overreaches.

how-i-learned-to-drive-2022.text: Vogel's Pulitzer-winning play about grooming and abuse remains a powerful, unsettling masterwork. Parker and Morse deliver incandescent performances in this sensitively directed revival, though some find the production overly cautious.

for-colored-girls-who-have-considered-su.text: Critics hail Camille A. Brown's thrilling revival as a triumphant Broadway homecoming, with exuberant choreography and powerful ensemble performances that make Shange's groundbreaking choreopoem feel both timeless and urgently contemporary.

hangmen-2022.text: McDonagh's pitch-black comedy about capital punishment delivers mordant wit and gallows humor, though some critics find it derivative of Pinter and less electric than his best work. Threlfall's performance anchors the darkly entertaining thriller.

funny-girl-2022.text: Critics are sharply divided on this long-awaited revival, with Beanie Feldstein's casting drawing harsh criticism for lacking vocal power, though Lea Michele's later takeover earns widespread praise for finally delivering the star quality the role demands.

the-skin-of-our-teeth-2022.text: Blain-Cruz's visually spectacular but uneven revival of Wilder's allegory dazzles with stunning design and ambition, yet struggles with tonal consistency and pacing, dividing critics between those captivated by its epic chaos and those exhausted by it.

a-strange-loop-2022.text: Critics hail this Pulitzer-winning musical as a radical, brazenly original work that's both brutally honest and electrifying, though some find its meta structure repetitious or self-indulgent. Most celebrate its groundbreaking voice on Broadway.

mr-saturday-night-2022.text: Crystal's charisma and comedy chops shine in this nostalgic but uneven musical adaptation, delivering laughs through Borscht Belt humor. Critics find it entertaining yet overstuffed and dated, working better as a comedy showcase than a fully realized musical.

macbeth-2022.text: Sam Gold's stylized production starring Daniel Craig and Ruth Negga draws mixed reviews, with critics praising the leads' performances but faulting the director's self-indulgent choices, bare staging, and lack of narrative drive that overshadows Shakespeare's tragedy.

girl-from-the-north-country-2022.text: McPherson's Depression-era drama weaves Dylan's songs into a haunting, unconventional musical that transcends the jukebox genre. Critics praise the gorgeous performances and atmospheric storytelling, though some find the narrative overstuffed or underwritten.

mrs-doubtfire-2021.text: Critics find this film-to-stage adaptation professionally executed but unnecessary, with Rob McClure's energetic performance unable to overcome a forgettable score and dated premise that struggles to justify its existence beyond family-friendly entertainment.

frankie-and-johnny-in-the-clair-de-lune-.text: McDonald and Shannon deliver powerful performances in this McNally revival, though some critics find the 1987 play overlong and dated. The stars' chemistry and raw authenticity mostly overcome the material's flaws in this compelling if imperfect production.

betrayal-2019.text: Jamie Lloyd's spare, stylish revival of Pinter's reverse-chronology infidelity drama earns strong praise for its surgical precision and emotional depth, with Hiddleston, Cox, and Ashton delivering exceptional performances in a stripped-down production.

the-height-of-the-storm-2019.text: Pryce and Atkins deliver transcendent performances in Zeller's puzzle-box meditation on aging and memory, though critics split on whether the playwright's trademark tricks enhance or overwhelm the emotional core.

the-great-society-2019.text: Brian Cox delivers a powerful performance as LBJ in this overstuffed sequel to "All the Way," but the sprawling historical drama struggles under the weight of too many events and characters, resulting in mixed critical reception.

linda-vista-2019.text: Tracy Letts' character study of a toxic middle-aged white man divides critics: some praise its sharp wit and honest portrayal of masculinity in crisis, while others question whether this self-absorbed protagonist merits nearly three hours of stage time.

the-rose-tattoo-2019.text: Critics are mixed on this Williams revival, praising Marisa Tomei's committed performance but faulting Trip Cullman's overly broad direction that miscalibrates the comedy-drama balance, resulting in a production that feels miscalibrated and emotionally hollow.

the-lightning-thief-2019.text: Critics are mixed on this energetic YA adaptation, praising its enthusiastic cast and colorful spirit but faulting thin storytelling, forgettable songs, and a lack of theatrical magic that leaves it feeling like "Harry Potter lite."

the-sound-inside-2019.text: Parker delivers a tour-de-force performance in Rapp's literary psychological thriller, though critics divide on whether the intimate two-hander's cerebral, dark storytelling justifies its Broadway venue.

tina-2019.text: Adrienne Warren delivers an electrifying, tour-de-force performance that elevates an otherwise formulaic jukebox bio-musical. Critics universally praise Warren's powerhouse vocals and charisma, though most find the by-the-book storytelling underwhelming.

the-inheritance-2019.text: Critics largely praise Lopez's ambitious seven-hour epic about gay men grappling with AIDS legacy and generational divides, though many find it overlong and indulgent. Strong performances and emotional power shine through sprawling structure.

a-christmas-carol-2019.text: Critics praise this ambitious adaptation for its stunning stagecraft and design, though reactions to its darker tone and storytelling choices are mixed. Jefferson Mays's solo performance and the production's technical wizardry earn widespread acclaim.

jagged-little-pill-2019.text: Critics find this Alanis Morissette jukebox musical earnest and ambitious but overstuffed, tackling numerous social issues with mixed results. Strong performances and powerful songs impress, though many cite a contrived plot and comparisons to "Next to Normal."

my-name-is-lucy-barton-2020.text: Critics are divided on this Strout adaptation, with Laura Linney's luminous solo performance universally praised but many finding the play itself underpowered and overly faithful to the novel, lacking theatrical vitality despite its quiet emotional resonance.

a-soldiers-play-2020.text: Critics praise this belated Broadway debut of Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama as timely and riveting, with strong performances from Underwood and Grier anchoring Leon's muscular direction, though some find the 1981 play more conventional than today's bold new voices.

grand-horizons-2020.text: Bess Wohl's sitcom-style comedy about a divorcing elderly couple earns mixed reviews. Critics praise the stellar performances by Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, but fault the play's familiar, middlebrow humor and shallow exploration of its themes.

west-side-story-2020.text: Van Hove's radical reimagining divides critics with its extensive video projections and new choreography replacing Robbins' iconic work. Some praise its bold, visceral modernity; others find it a muddled, pretentious mess that overwhelms the story.

whos-afraid-of-virginia-woolf-2020.text: Metcalf and Everett deliver fierce performances in Albee's masterpiece, though the production occasionally feels calculated rather than truly devastating.

the-boys-in-the-band-2018.text: This star-studded 50th anniversary revival earns praise for its superb ensemble cast and Joe Mantello's sensitive direction, though critics debate whether Crowley's groundbreaking 1968 play feels dated or timeless in today's context.

straight-white-men-2018.text: Critics are mixed on Young Jean Lee's historic Broadway debut, praising the strong ensemble cast and comedic moments but finding the examination of privilege more lecture than drama, with an unsatisfying structure and ambiguous resolution.

head-over-heels-2018.text: Critics are divided on this Go-Go's jukebox musical set to an Elizabethan tale, with most finding it a silly, energetic romp that celebrates LGBTQ inclusivity, though some dismiss the mismatched concept as overwrought and forgettable.

gettin-the-band-back-together-2018.text: Critics find this original rock musical tacky and formulaic, with predictable plotting and forgettable songs, though its energetic cast and good-natured charm win over some viewers willing to embrace its unabashed schlock.

pretty-woman-the-musical-2018.text: Critics find Pretty Woman: The Musical a competent but uninspired adaptation with forgettable songs and dated gender politics. Strong performances from the leads can't overcome a bland Bryan Adams score and overly faithful screenplay that adds little to the beloved film.

bernhardthamlet-2018.text: McTeer delivers a commanding, charismatic performance as Sarah Bernhardt, but Rebeck's play divides critics with its uneven structure, preachy dialogue, and overly talky stretches that undermine an otherwise timely feminist premise.

the-nap-2018.text: Critics are divided on this British snooker comedy, with some praising Bean's witty dialogue and oddball characters, while others find it unfunny and slow-paced. American actors' struggling accents are a frequent complaint.

the-lifespan-of-a-fact-2018.text: Critics find this journalism ethics play smart and timely, elevated by stellar performances from Radcliffe, Jones, and Cannavale. However, many note the 85-minute show feels thin or underdeveloped despite its provocative premise.

the-ferryman-2018.text: Critics hail Butterworth's epic Irish family drama as a sprawling masterpiece with stunning ensemble work and Mendes' brilliant direction. Though some find it overlong or clichéd, most praise its thrilling storytelling and emotional power during The Troubles.

the-waverly-gallery-2018.text: Critics praise Elaine May's triumphant Broadway return at 86, delivering a heartbreaking, masterful performance as a woman with dementia in Lonergan's memory play, though some find the work itself underwhelming compared to her towering achievement.

torch-song-2018.text: Critics praise Michael Urie's powerhouse performance in this revival of Fierstein's landmark play, finding it still relevant and moving. However, some feel the production can't escape comparisons to Fierstein's original and lacks its full fire.

american-son-2018.text: Critics praise Kerry Washington's riveting performance in this timely racial drama about a mother searching for her missing son, but find the play itself heavy-handed and didactic, with characters that feel more like debate points than flesh-and-blood people.

king-kong-2018.text: Critics praise the spectacular 20-foot puppet as a technical marvel, but find the musical surrounding Kong disappointing, with forgettable songs, a weak book, and hollow storytelling that fails to match the creature's impressive stagecraft.

the-new-one-2018.text: Critics embrace Birbiglia's deeply personal, hilarious exploration of reluctant fatherhood, praising his gift for balancing humor with genuine emotion and making the neurotic journey universally relatable, though some find the material uneven.

the-prom-2018.text: Critics largely embrace "The Prom" as a joyful, old-fashioned musical comedy with infectious energy and heart, praising its sharp Broadway satire and standout performances.

the-cher-show-2018.text: Critics find "The Cher Show" a glitzy, entertaining spectacle that delivers crowd-pleasing hits and dazzling Bob Mackie costumes, but suffers from a shallow, rushed book typical of jukebox bios. Stephanie J. Block's performance as older Cher earns widespread praise.

network-2018.text: Critics praise Bryan Cranston's powerhouse performance in this multimedia-heavy adaptation, but reactions to Ivo van Hove's high-tech staging are mixed—some find it thrilling and timely, others feel the spectacle overwhelms the human drama.

to-kill-a-mockingbird-2018.text: Sorkin's adaptation earns mostly positive reviews for its theatrical power and contemporary relevance, with Jeff Daniels' nuanced Atticus Finch widely praised. Critics split on whether changes honor or dilute Lee's novel.

choir-boy-2019.text: Critics praise McCraney's lyrical coming-of-age drama and Jeremy Pope's star-making performance, with gorgeous spiritual singing earning raves. Some find the structure uneven and characters underdeveloped, but most celebrate its necessary Broadway representation.

true-west-2019.text: Critics are divided on this Shepard revival: Hawke and Dano's performances earn praise for their intensity, but the production itself receives mixed reviews, with some finding it a "ripping revival" while others deem it "tedious" and "disappointing."

be-more-chill-2019.text: Critics are divided on this viral sensation's Broadway transfer: some praise its energetic score and youthful appeal, while others find it frenetic and aimed squarely at teens, with older audiences likely left cold by its manic energy.

kiss-me-kate-2019.text: O'Hara's glorious vocals lead this entertaining revival, though critics split on whether Ellis's direction brings enough energy to Porter's classic score. Carlyle's choreography dazzles, but some find the production uneven despite successful updates to dated gender politics.

aint-too-proud-2019.text: Critics find "Ain't Too Proud" an entertaining jukebox musical elevated by exceptional performances and irresistible music, though most agree the conventional book and shallow character development keep it from reaching its full dramatic potential.

what-the-constitution-means-to-me-2019.text: Critics hail Schreck's genre-defying work as a powerful blend of memoir, civics lesson, and political theater that turns constitutional debate into something deeply personal and urgent, though a few find its structure overly casual or its emotional impact diluted.

king-lear-2019.text: Jackson delivers a commanding, technically impressive performance at 82, but Gold's cluttered, uneven production undermines the tragedy with distracting gimmicks and inconsistent direction that fails to cohere.

oklahoma-2019.text: Fish's stripped-down revival excavates the darkness and sexuality lurking beneath the classic, dividing audiences with its daring reimagining. Most critics praise the fresh perspective and intimate staging, though some find it pretentious and a few purists are outraged.

burn-this-2019.text: Driver delivers a volcanic, tour-de-force performance that electrifies Wilson's 1987 drama, but the revival receives mixed notices overall.

hillary-and-clinton-2019.text: Metcalf and Lithgow deliver stellar performances in this smart but slight speculative drama about the Clintons' marriage during the 2008 primaries, though critics find it lacks fresh insights and dramatic urgency.

gary-a-sequel-to-titus-andronicus-2019.text: Critics are divided on Taylor Mac's audacious, blood-soaked comedy: some praise Lane's performance and the play's philosophical ambition amid the gross-out humor, while others find it labored and thin despite its talented cast.

all-my-sons-2019.text: Critics mostly praise this powerful revival of Miller's classic, with Bening and Letts delivering compelling performances that elevate the production's moral urgency and contemporary relevance.

tootsie-2019.text: Critics praise "Tootsie" as Broadway's funniest new musical with a hilarious, smartly updated book by Robert Horn and star Santino Fontana's powerhouse performance, though most agree David Yazbek's score is forgettable and can't match the comedy gold.

ink-2019.text: Graham's energetic drama about Murdoch's tabloid revolution crackles with theatrical flair and powerhouse performances from Carvel and Miller, though critics split on whether it's substantive storytelling or stylish spectacle that lacks depth.

beetlejuice-2019.text: Critics are divided on this manic, visually spectacular adaptation—some find it chaotic fun with eye-popping design and energetic performances, while others dismiss it as exhaustingly crass and forgettable despite Brightman's committed lead turn.

1984-2017.text: Critics praise this visceral, harrowing adaptation as timely and theatrically powerful, though some find its brutal, sensory-assault approach overwhelming. The intense torture scenes prove genuinely frightening, but style occasionally overshadows substance.

the-terms-of-my-surrender-2017.text: Moore's anti-Trump Broadway debut divides critics as more political rally than theater. Fans find it entertaining and energizing, but detractors cite self-indulgence and preaching to the choir, with most agreeing it's slickly staged yet overlong.

prince-of-broadway-2017.text: Critics praise the talented nine-member cast and stellar musical performances from Prince's iconic shows, but fault the shallow book that fails to illuminate the legendary director's creative process, resulting in an entertaining yet formulaic greatest-hits revue.

time-and-the-conways-2017.text: Critics are mixed on this Priestley revival, praising strong performances and elegant design but finding the 1937 drawing-room drama dated and static, with philosophical concepts more interesting than the actual drama.

m-butterfly-2017.text: Critics find this revival of Hwang's Tony-winning play disappointing, citing Taymor's fussy direction, extensive script revisions, and lack of chemistry between Owen and Ha.

junk-2017.text: Critics find Akhtar's ambitious financial drama smart and fast-paced with strong performances, but overly familiar and emotionally cold.

the-bands-visit-2017.text: Critics hail this intimate musical as a quietly ravishing miracle that finds profound beauty in small moments. Yazbek's exquisite Middle Eastern-flavored score, Cromer's sensitive direction, and superb ensemble work create a gentle, deeply moving meditation on human connection.

latin-history-for-morons-2017.text: Critics praise Leguizamo's energetic performance and comic mastery, but find the show disjointed and overlong. His personal storytelling and political urgency resonate, though the history lesson lacks focus and sharp editing would help.

meteor-shower-2017.text: Critics find Steve Martin's absurdist comedy a lightweight, sketch-like trifle that's often funny but lacks substance. Amy Schumer and the talented cast earn praise for wringing laughs from a thin, repetitive script that never coheres into a satisfying play.

the-parisian-woman-2017.text: Critics find Willimon's Trump-era political drama disappointingly thin and stilted, with wooden dialogue and dated theatrics undermining Uma Thurman's commanding Broadway debut. Blair Brown's supporting turn earns more praise than the contrived plot.

once-on-this-island-2017.text: Critics hail this revival as a radiant, joyful reimagining, with Michael Arden's immersive staging and Camille Brown's choreography transforming Circle in the Square into a Caribbean wonderland.

spongebob-squarepants-2017.text: Critics find SpongeBob SquarePants a surprisingly joyful spectacle with dazzling design and infectious energy, though some note an overstuffed book and uneven score. Ethan Slater's star-making performance and psychedelic stagecraft win over skeptics.

the-children-2017.text: Critics praise Lucy Kirkwood's thought-provoking post-apocalyptic drama for its stellar British cast and timely themes about generational responsibility, though some find its pacing glacial and plotting uneven.

farinelli-and-the-king-2017.text: Rylance delivers a masterful, tour-de-force performance as the mad Spanish king, elevating van Kampen's thin, meandering debut play. Gorgeous Handel arias and candlelit atmosphere enchant, but the slim plot tests patience.

john-lithgow-stories-by-heart-2018.text: Critics find Lithgow's storytelling warm and masterful, with his vocal dexterity and charm earning consistent praise, but many question whether the modest material justifies a Broadway outing, finding the personal anecdotes more engaging than the stories themselves.

escape-to-margaritaville-2018.text: Critics find this Jimmy Buffett jukebox musical a lightweight, predictable diversion with a corny plot and cardboard characters, though the talented cast and catchy songs provide breezy fun for Parrotheads willing to check their brains at the door.

frozen-2018.text: Critics are mixed on Disney's "Frozen" Broadway adaptation, praising strong performances and spectacle but finding it uninspired compared to "The Lion King." New songs disappoint, and the thin plot feels padded, though fans of the film will likely enjoy it.

lobby-hero-2018.text: Lonergan's morally complex drama feels strikingly timely in this stellar revival, with critics praising the four-actor ensemble—particularly Brian Tyree Henry—and sharp dialogue, though some find the pacing uneven and tone occasionally off-balance.

three-tall-women-2018.text: Critics hail Glenda Jackson's commanding, triumphant Broadway return in this superb revival of Albee's Pulitzer winner, with stellar support from Metcalf and Pill. Joe Mantello's direction illuminates the play's dark humor and brutal honesty about aging and mortality.

mean-girls-2018.text: Critics find Mean Girls an entertaining but uneven adaptation that captures Tina Fey's sharp wit and benefits from an energetic cast, though the score is often deemed forgettable and the production occasionally lacks the film's satirical bite.

children-of-a-lesser-god-2018.text: Mixed reviews praise Lauren Ridloff's fierce, luminous performance, but critics find the 1980 play dated and the revival uneven, with Joshua Jackson's work dividing opinion and Kenny Leon's direction often called heavy-handed or lightweight.

carousel-2018.text: Joshua Henry delivers a powerhouse performance in this handsome but uneven revival that boasts glorious singing and thrilling choreography, yet struggles with the show's dated treatment of domestic violence and lacks a clear directorial vision.

my-fair-lady-2018.text: Bartlett Sher's sumptuous Lincoln Center revival earns widespread praise for its elegant production values and fresh perspective on the classic, though some critics find the leads lackluster and the staging overly traditional.

summer-2018.text: Critics find this jukebox musical as unimaginative as its title, with a threadbare book that reduces Summer's life to a Wikipedia page. The saving grace: powerhouse vocals from three talented leads and infectious disco hits that still make audiences move.

travesties-2018.text: Critics hail this "sparkling" and "dazzling" Stoppard revival for its brilliant wordplay and Patrick Marber's pitch-perfect direction. Tom Hollander's performance dazzles, though some find the dense, reference-heavy comedy challenging to follow.

saint-joan-2018.text: Critics find Condola Rashad a luminous, charismatic presence in this handsome but stolid Shaw revival that's praised for its stellar cast and intelligent staging, yet criticized for feeling overlong, dramatically inert, and lacking the fire to fully ignite.

the-iceman-cometh-2018.text: Critics praise Denzel Washington's powerful performance and George C. Wolfe's energetic direction of O'Neill's epic, though some find the four-hour runtime taxing. The stellar ensemble cast earns widespread acclaim in this mostly well-received revival.

cirque-du-soleil-paramour-2016.text: Cirque du Soleil's Broadway debut dazzles with spectacular acrobatics but stumbles badly with its weak, clichéd musical theater story—a visually stunning production that can't successfully merge circus artistry with traditional book musical storytelling.

an-act-of-god-2016.text: Critics find this irreverent comedy intermittently amusing but one-note and repetitive, with charismatic star turns from Jim Parsons and Sean Hayes elevating material that feels more like a stretched sketch than a full Broadway show.

motown-the-musical-2016.text: Critics find the iconic Motown songs irresistible and performances electric, but fault Berry Gordy's self-serving, superficial book for being unfocused and dramatically hollow, cramming too many hits into a clunky narrative.

cats-2016.text: Critics remain divided on this revival, with fans satisfied but skeptics unconvinced. The spectacle and catchy score earn praise, though many note the show's thin plot and dated feel, calling it entertaining kitsch that's impossible to take seriously.

the-encounter-2016.text: Critics are sharply divided on this binaural audio experiment: some hail McBurney's innovative sound design as "extraordinary" and "transfixing," while others find the two-hour solo show tedious, calling it better suited to a podcast than Broadway.

holiday-inn-the-new-irving-berlin-musica.text: Critics find this old-fashioned Irving Berlin musical a cheerful, nostalgic diversion with spectacular tap choreography and a treasure trove of classic songs, though most agree the featherweight plot and predictable book are merely vehicles for the show-stopping dance numbers.

oh-hello-on-broadway-2016.text: Kroll and Mulaney's extended sketch about two cranky Upper West Side geezers draws mostly positive reviews for its absurdist humor and sharp character work, though some critics find the premise thin for a full Broadway run.

heisenberg-2016.text: Parker dazzles in this minimalist two-hander, but critics split on Stephens' slim romantic premise. Some find it quirky, tender and beautifully acted; others call it implausible, underwritten and exhausting at just 80 minutes.

the-cherry-orchard-2016.text: This revival of Chekhov's classic draws mixed-to-negative reviews, with critics calling it disjointed, flat, and dramatically underdeveloped. Diane Lane's performance earns praise, but the production fails to capture the play's delicate tragicomic balance.

the-front-page-2016.text: Critics are mixed on this star-studded revival of the 1928 newspaper farce, praising Nathan Lane's electrifying performance but noting he doesn't appear until halfway through. The first act drags, though the ensemble cast and Jack O'Brien's direction earn acclaim.

falsettos-2016.text: Critics largely embrace this heartfelt revival, praising Finn's intricate score and the stellar cast's performances, though some find the material dated. The devastating second act exploring AIDS resonates powerfully despite occasional pacing issues.

les-liaisons-dangereuses-2016.text: Reviews are mixed on this stylish revival. Janet McTeer earns widespread praise for her commanding Marquise, but critics are divided on Schreiber's Valmont and the production's lack of heat, with many finding it visually gorgeous yet emotionally cold.

natasha-pierre-and-the-great-comet-of-18.text: Critics hail this immersive electro-pop opera as a thrilling theatrical spectacle with stunning stagecraft and inventive direction. Malloy's score and the transformed Imperial Theatre dazzle, though some find the first act drags and emotional depth occasionally lacking.

a-bronx-tale-the-musical-2016.text: Critics find this familiar coming-of-age tale a crowd-pleasing but unexceptional musical adaptation, elevated by strong performances and Alan Menken's tuneful score, though many question whether the well-worn story needed musicalization.

dear-evan-hansen-2016.text: Critics hail this smart, deeply felt musical about teen isolation and social media as extraordinary, powered by Ben Platt's astonishing star-making performance and Pasek & Paul's strongest score to date, though some find the ending too neat.

in-transit-2016.text: Critics are mixed on Broadway's first a cappella musical, praising the impressive vocal arrangements and energetic performances but faulting the predictable stories and stereotypical characters that never fully engage.

the-present-2017.text: Critics are divided on this Chekhov adaptation, with Blanchett's magnetic performance earning widespread praise while the three-hour production itself draws mixed reactions, ranging from "dazzling" to "crushing bore."

jitney-2017.text: Wilson's final Century Cycle play reaches Broadway in a triumphant production featuring superb ensemble work and Santiago-Hudson's masterful direction.

sunset-boulevard-2017.text: Critics are divided on this revival, with praise centering on the lead performance—particularly the vocal power and intensity—though some find the stripped-down, video-heavy staging either thrillingly inventive or distractingly gimmicky.

sunday-in-the-park-with-george-2017.text: Critics widely praise this stripped-down revival for its emotional clarity and exceptional performances, particularly Gyllenhaal's surprisingly strong musical debut and Ashford's luminous work, though some miss the visual spectacle of previous productions.

significant-other-2017.text: Harmon's comedy-drama about a lonely gay millennial watching friends marry earns praise for Gideon Glick's exceptional lead performance and sharp humor, though critics split on whether the familiar premise offers enough depth beyond its witty surface.

the-glass-menagerie-2017.text: Critics are divided on Sam Gold's stripped-down revival, praising Sally Field's fierce, unsentimental Amanda but questioning the stark, deconstructed approach that polarizes as much as it illuminates Williams' classic.

come-from-away-2017.text: Critics embrace this feel-good 9/11 musical about Newfoundland hospitality as heartwarming and uplifting, praising its ensemble cast and swift staging. Some find it overly sentimental with repetitive songs, but most celebrate its moving testament to human kindness.

the-price-2017.text: Critics praise this solid revival of Miller's lesser-known play, with Danny DeVito stealing the show in his Broadway debut. While Shalhoub and Hecht impress, Ruffalo struggles initially, and the play itself is deemed slow and talky despite timeless themes.

miss-saigon-2017.text: The lavish revival delivers spectacular production values—especially that iconic helicopter—and strong vocal performances, but critics are divided on its dated, melodramatic storytelling and problematic racial stereotypes that feel increasingly uncomfortable with time.

sweat-2017.text: Nottage's timely drama about working-class America earns strong praise for its compassionate character work and powerful ensemble, though some critics find it schematic and heavy-handed in execution.

the-play-that-goes-wrong-2017.text: Critics largely embrace this British slapstick farce as expertly executed physical comedy, though some find the relentless chaos exhausting. Most praise the precision timing and theatrical ingenuity, even if the humor feels silly and one-note.

amelie-a-new-musical-2017.text: Critics find this whimsical adaptation charming but ultimately weightless, struggling to translate the film's cinematic magic to stage. Phillipa Soo and the visual design earn praise, but the show feels precious and exhausting in its effort to enchant.

present-laughter-2017.text: Kevin Kline dazzles in this stylish but safe revival of Coward's comedy, with critics praising his physical comedy and star quality while finding the production occasionally plodding and the 1939 material somewhat dated.

war-paint-2017.text: LuPone and Ebersole deliver powerhouse performances as cosmetics rivals Rubinstein and Arden, but critics find the musical itself disappointingly bland, with forgettable songs and a thin book that never fully ignites despite its glamorous production values.

oslo-2017.text: Critics praise this riveting political thriller about the 1993 Oslo Accords as gripping and surprisingly entertaining despite its three-hour runtime. Strong ensemble performances and Bartlett Sher's direction elevate the talky, complex material into absorbing drama.

groundhog-day-2017.text: Critics generally praise this inventive musical adaptation, with Andy Karl's charismatic performance and clever staging earning acclaim, though some find Tim Minchin's score unmemorable and the show overlong or repetitive despite its theatrical ingenuity.

indecent-2017.text: Paula Vogel's Broadway debut earns widespread acclaim for its powerful, theatrically inventive telling of a controversial Yiddish play's history. Critics praise the moving ensemble work and imaginative staging, though some find the sprawling narrative overstuffed.

the-little-foxes-2017.text: Linney and Nixon's role-switching anchors Sullivan's sharp revival of Hellman's Southern melodrama, earning widespread praise for strong performances and timeless themes, though some question if the production breaks new ground.

hello-dolly-2017.text: Critics hail this lavish revival as a triumph of old-fashioned musical theater, with Bette Midler's brassy comic genius earning raves despite vocal limitations. Bernadette Peters brings warmth and vocal polish as her successor.

charlie-and-the-chocolate-factory-2017.text: Critics found this Broadway adaptation disappointing despite Christian Borle's energetic performance as Wonka. Reviews cite a lackluster score, bloated first act, and diminished spectacle from the London production, though kids may still enjoy it.

anastasia-2017.text: Critics find "Anastasia" a visually sumptuous but narratively uneven spectacle. The lavish production values and Christy Altomare's performance earn praise, while the overstretched story and forgettable score disappoint in this nostalgic throwback musical.

six-degrees-of-separation-2017.text: Critics praise Guare's sharp play as still-relevant and Janney's commanding performance, but many find Cullman's direction too broad and farcical, sacrificing emotional depth for laughs and leaving the tone uneven.

bandstand-2017.text: Critics praise Blankenbuehler's electrifying choreography and the talented cast, but find this WWII veterans musical tonally uneven—struggling to balance crowd-pleasing swing numbers with its darker PTSD themes and hampered by a forgettable score.

a-dolls-house-part-2-2017.text: Lucas Hnath's clever, funny sequel to Ibsen's classic earns widespread praise for its sharp writing and stellar performances, particularly Laurie Metcalf's commanding Nora. Critics find it smart and thought-provoking, though some note it lacks the original's depth.

amazing-grace-2015.text: Critics find "Amazing Grace" well-intentioned but dramatically uneven, praising its strong cast and production values while faulting its bland score and wooden storytelling that fails to match the power of its slavery-to-redemption subject matter.

spring-awakening-2015.text: This innovative Deaf West revival energizes the 2006 Tony winner by integrating ASL and mixing deaf and hearing actors, creating a thrilling, accessible production that deepens themes of teen alienation and communication.

old-times-2015.text: Mixed-to-positive reviews praise the "superb" performances, especially Owen, Best, and Reilly's perfectly pitched trio, but critics divide sharply on director Hodge's stylized, tech-heavy staging—some find it compelling, others call it pretentious and distracting from Pinter's te

fool-for-love-2015.text: Critics praise Rockwell and Arianda's fierce performances in this raw Shepard revival, but opinions split on whether the 32-year-old play retains its power, with some finding it visceral and others feeling it lacks heat and intimacy.

the-gin-game-2015.text: Jones and Tyson deliver masterful performances that elevate D.L. Coburn's slight, schematic Pulitzer winner, though critics find the play itself has aged poorly and the ending falls flat despite the stars' undeniable chemistry.

dames-at-sea-2015.text: Critics are split on this featherweight 1960s spoof of Depression-era movie musicals, praising the talented cast's tap-dancing prowess but questioning whether the dated material belongs on Broadway at all.

sylvia-2015.text: Critics praise Annaleigh Ashford's delightful performance as the titular canine in Gurney's charming but lightweight comedy, though most find the 1995 play thin and inconsequential despite its crowd-pleasing humor.

therese-raquin-2015.text: Critics find this Broadway revival of "Thérèse Raquin" dramatically inert and sluggish despite Knightley's committed performance and striking design. The production earns praise for its visual elements but criticism for its slow pace and lack of dramatic vitality.

king-charles-iii-2015.text: Critics praise Bartlett's audacious Shakespearean verse and Pigott-Smith's commanding performance, calling it clever, provocative theater. While most find it riveting and brilliantly conceived, some question its credibility and relevance for American audiences.

on-your-feet-2015.text: This energetic jukebox musical delivers infectious Latin rhythms and crowd-pleasing choreography, though critics find the formulaic book and TV-movie storytelling predictable. The music and performances win over audiences despite dramatic shortcomings.
